posts.name: cmschex
posts.cooked:
The difference between this and the first $20 increase for the expansion minis is that the stretch goals added content to both those who did and didn't pledge at the increased levels, leading to a funding model where enough stuff was unlocked to make it a no-brainer for people to increase their pledges (if they wanted minis).  This current increase is asking for twice that amount, includes both minis and scenarios (which potentially alienates people who don't want the minis), and is relying entirely on attracting enough new backers to reach the stretch goals to make it worth the price of the addon.  It looks likely to get that way, but I've seen stranger things happen on KS.  The real downside is that if it only hits 1 or 2 more stretch goals and the value isn't there, then people who have increased for this tier on speculation of future goals will (I am assuming) drop from this tier, which will dramatically alter the funding in the last hour.

 

I'm not saying that this option, will, in the long run, be a bad deal.  But right now it is, and I just wanted to make the points that regardless of the business sense of the approach, the way this has all been communicated has obvioiusly left a negative impression on a fair number of people

I absolutely disagree with the idea of Kickstarter exclusives.

It's unfair for international people who have to pay so much extra for shipping, and it's unfair for those people who don't discover the game until after the Kickstarter finishes, or who just can't afford it right now. Why should they miss out on the cool stuff?

I've probably said this before, but I can't understand the mentality of people who want their nice things to be owned by fewer people. Do you really take more pleasure in your shinies if Joe Bloggs is denied them? I want as many people to have the fun stuff. Apart from the question of fairness, exclusives make bad business sense. Why? Because so many people will decline to buy the game at retail if they see it as "incomplete". Sure, exclusives might make the Kickstarter campaign more successful but you've got to look at this long-term.
